Is your medicine genuine? One scan answers it.

The whole loop

From the packaging line to the patient's phone

Every pack carries one unique, non-sequential code. The code's whole life is visible in the dashboard, and every check a patient makes feeds the security team's queue.

1 · ProductCreate the medicine; its SKU starts every code.
2 · BatchPlan a production run and issue its codes.
3 · PrintExport CSV for the line, or print label sheets.
4 · ReleasePacks ship; codes become checkable.
5 · Patient scansCamera or typed code - verdict in seconds.
6 · Team reviewsDuplicates, unknown codes and bursts raise alerts.
Recall, any timeA recalled batch flags every later scan of its packs.

Genuine

The code exists, is released, and this is its first verification - green, with the leaflet.

Flagged

Already verified elsewhere, recalled, expired or unknown - red, with a report form.

Check the code

A typo is never called counterfeit - amber asks the patient to retype it.

Getting started

Admin · Security · Regulatororbitqrcode.vercel.app/login

The dashboard lives at orbitqrcode.vercel.app/admin; signing in is the only door. The public portal needs no account at all.

Sign in

  1. Open orbitqrcode.vercel.app/login - or press "Back to portal" to reach the public side instead.
  2. Work email and password. Accounts are created by an administrator on the Users page.
  3. Forgot the password? There is no self-service reset - ask an administrator, who sets a temporary one you must change at the next sign-in.

Sessions expire on their own; the account panel lists every open session, and changing the password signs out every other device.

Your account top-right picture, or the chip at the sidebar's foot

  • Role, granted permissions, last sign-in.
  • Change the password - at least 12 characters with upper case, lower case and a digit.
  • Open sessions, each with its expiry; changing the password revokes all the others.

Finding your way

  • The sidebar is grouped the way the work is grouped: Monitor, Investigate, Manage, Governance.
  • Red badges on Alerts and Patient reports count what still needs someone.
  • The sidebar shows only what your role can open - a regulator's is four entries long.
  • Theme toggle and sign-out sit top-right, beside the clock.
2

The guided tour

Admin · Security · Regulatorreplay: /admin/settings

On the very first sign-in the dashboard walks each person through itself: the page dims, one section at a time is lit and ringed, and a card beside it says what that section is for.

How it behaves

  • Opens by itself the first time an account signs in - nothing to find or press.
  • Spotlights the real interface. Each step highlights the actual sidebar entry it is explaining; the card points at it with an arrow.
  • Role-aware. Someone without Alerts or Users simply never gets those steps - the tour never points at something that is not there.
  • Remembered on the account. Finishing or skipping records it server-side, so it does not reopen on another device.
  • Keyboard friendly. → next, ← back, Esc finish.

The route, step by step

  1. Welcome - greets the person by name: "Here is a quick look at where everything is in the dashboard. It takes about a minute."
  2. Overview - "Your home screen: the last 30 days of checks, flagged packs and what needs attention, at a glance."
  3. Alerts - "Suspicious scans wait here for someone to review them. The red count is how many are still open."
  4. Scan log - "Every verification attempt, genuine or not - when, where, and through which channel."
  5. Patient reports - "Packs that patients and pharmacists have reported to you directly."
  6. Code lookup - "Type any pack code to see its product, batch, status and every time it was checked."
  7. Products - "The catalogue. A product's SKU starts every code issued for it."
  8. Batches & codes - "Plan a production batch, issue its codes, and move it from printed to released."
  9. Audit log - "Every change anyone makes in the dashboard is recorded here, and can never be edited."
  10. Users - "Add staff accounts and choose what each person can see and do."
  11. Settings - "Portal notices, support numbers and alert thresholds - and your own profile."
  12. Theme, sign out and your account - the tools in the top-right corner.
  13. You are all set - "You can take this tour again at any time from Settings."

Replaying it

  1. Open Settings → Your profile.
  2. Press "Take the tour again" - top-right of the profile card. open Settings live

During a demo this button is the fastest way to show the tour on the live system - press it and let the audience watch the dashboard introduce itself.

3

The patient portal

Patients · Pharmacists · anyoneorbitqrcode.vercel.app

No account, no app. Scan the QR on the pack or type the code from under the scratch panel, and get a plain-language verdict: genuine, do not use, or check the code you typed.

Say who you are - once per phone

  • Full name, mobile number, email, and whether you are the patient, a pharmacist or a caregiver. City is optional.
  • The point: a pack that later proves counterfeit or recalled can be followed up with the person who checked it.
  • A privacy notice spells out what is kept, why, who sees it, and how to have it removed.
  • Staff can switch the whole gate off from Settings (portal.require_details).

Check a pack

  1. Scan the QR code - the camera opens right in the browser - or type the code printed under the scratch panel.
  2. Check this pack. The verdict arrives in seconds.
  3. Read the result - and the leaflet, if the pack is genuine.
  4. Report a problem with any pack, whatever the scan said.
Genuine - first verificationDo not use - duplicate, unknown, recalled or expiredCheck the code - looks like a typo

Re-checking the same pack on the same phone stays genuine - a patient who refreshes, or shows a pharmacist, must not be told their medicine is fake. Repeat checks from the same source inside 15 minutes count as one verification.

A mistyped code is never called counterfeit. Checksum failures get their own amber "check the code" result.

Three more doors

  • QR deep link /v/<code> - scanning a printed pack QR with the phone's own camera lands straight on that code's verdict.
  • Leaflet QR /leaflet/<sku> - product information only, no authenticity claim, versioned so an old box still shows its own leaflet.
  • SMS - text the code to the shortcode (Settings holds the number) where there is no data connection.
4

Overview

Admin · Security · Regulator/admin

The home screen: the last 30 days of checks, flagged packs and what needs attention, at a glance. Pilot and sandbox batches are excluded from every figure.

What is on it

  • Checks - total verifications, with today's count and the previous 30 days for trend.
  • Flagged - how many checks were flagged, and the rate per 1,000.
  • Needs attention - open alerts, with how many are high or critical.
  • Units serialized - codes issued, and how many a patient has verified.
  • Verification volume - genuine against flagged, day by day.
  • Where checks come from and batches with the most flags - the two places an outbreak shows first.
  • Legend - top-right, explains every sidebar icon this person sees.
5

Alerts, scans, reports, customers

Admin · Security/admin/alerts

The Monitor group is where suspicious activity surfaces and gets worked, and where every check and every checker is on record.

Alerts the red badge counts what is open open live

Suspicious verifications queued for review. Flagging never triggers an automatic recall - a person always decides.

  • What raises one: a code verified twice from different devices, an unknown code, a scan of a recalled batch, or a burst of guessed codes from one source.
  • Working one: open it, see the code, the scans behind it and the person who checked; move it open → investigating → resolved or dismissed, with notes.
  • Severity: high and critical float to the top and are counted on the Overview.

Scan log open live

Every verification attempt. Locations are approximate; web checks name the person who gave their details on the portal.

  • Columns: when, code, product, result, reason, channel, who checked, where.
  • Filter by result and channel; pilot scans are excluded unless asked for.
  • Export CSV takes the filtered log with you.

Patient reports badge counts new ones open live

Suspect packs reported directly by patients and pharmacists - with the reporter's contact details and where they bought the pack, so the team can call back and trace the outlet.

Customers open live

Who has been checking medicines on the portal, and how to reach them. This list exists because the portal asks who is checking - it is the follow-up channel when a pack proves unsafe.

6

Code lookup

Admin · Security/admin/lookup

Trace a single unit code through its entire history - the page an investigation starts on.

Using it

  1. Paste the code. Case and separators do not matter; a full QR URL also works.
  2. Read the unit's card: product, SKU, batch and its status, the code's own status, unit number in the run, manufacture and expiry dates.
  3. Scroll its history: total checks, successful verifications, first and last check - then every scan, one by one.

An alert names a code; paste it here and the whole story is on one page.

Products open live

8

Batches & codes

Admin · Security write · Regulator read/admin/batches

Every production run, the codes issued for it, and where it sits in its lifecycle.

The lifecycle

plannedthe run exists on paper
codes issuedone unique code per unit
printedthe line has the labels
releasedpacks ship - codes now verify
distributedout in the market
recalledfrom any live state - every later scan flags

Codes are non-sequential on purpose: knowing one tells a counterfeiter nothing about the next. Guessing bursts raise their own alert.

Issuing and printing

  1. Plan the batch - product, batch number, size, manufacture and expiry dates.
  2. Issue codes - the registry creates one per unit.
  3. Export CSV for the packaging line's printer, or print label sheets with real scannable QRs.
  4. Advance the status as the run moves - each change lands in the audit log.
9

Compliance & audit

Compliance: all · Audit: Admin, Security/admin/compliance

The two pages that make the system defensible: aggregate reporting for the regulator, and an append-only record of everything the team does.

Compliance open live

  • Serialization and verification totals for track-and-trace reporting.
  • No individual patient data is included - the regulator role cannot read single scan rows even by typing the URL; the API refuses.

Audit log open live

  • Every state-changing action taken in the dashboard - who, what, when, on which record, from which address.
  • Append-only: entries can never be edited or deleted, by anyone.
10

Users & settings

Administrator/admin/users

Staff accounts - patients and pharmacists never need one - and the runtime configuration the team can change without a deploy.

Users open live

  1. Add a person: name, work email, role. They get a temporary password and must change it at first sign-in.
  2. Pick the role: admin, security or regulator - the role is the whole permission set.
  3. Suspend, not delete: suspending revokes every session at once and keeps history intact. The last active administrator cannot be demoted or suspended.
  4. Reset a password when someone is locked out.

Settings open live

  • Your profile - picture, display name, and "Take the tour again".
  • Portal notice (portal.banner) - e.g. a recall notice at the top of the public page.
  • Support phone - shown to patients on a "do not use" result.
  • SMS shortcode - the number patients text a code to with no internet.
  • Details gate (portal.require_details) - whether the portal asks who is checking.
  • Alert thresholds and the other values the team tunes without a deploy.
